```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.6, dpi = 110,
  warning = FALSE
)
```

After the raising (vignette **2**) every stratum has a weight of landings and
of discards, but a length (or age) distribution only where somebody measured
fish. The **allocation** gives every stratum one: a stratum without samples
takes the distribution of the samples of its group. This vignette follows the
whole step on the brill data - look at where the samples are, write the groups,
check them, allocate, look at what the allocation did, add it up into catch
at length, and write it in the format of the stock coordination; the last
section lets the data choose the groups instead. It is a
walkthrough, not a test: nothing here asserts pass or fail, and it is the
script to run chunk by chunk in RStudio.

It is driven directly with the vendored RDBESStockCoord functions -
`check_group_conditions()`, `catchAllocationAoL()`, `catchAtAoLAggregation()`
and `meanWoLatAoLAggregation()` - the same pattern ICES's own scripts use; the
stock coordination files are made by `catchCombined()` and
`distributionsCombined()`. Ages are allocated exactly the same way with
`distributionType = "Age"`.

# Data and the raised catch

Brill, `bll.27.3a47de`, 2025, from the CEF csv files under
`inst/extdata/data_CEF_format` (local to this machine; the files are not in the
repository). The incidental-bycatch strata and BMS are left out to keep the
example short: the first has no discard estimate to raise from, the second has
its own raising.

```{r load, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(rcef)

cef_dir <- file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", "data_CEF_format")

# blank cells (no discard domain, no trip count ...) read as NA
catch_data <- read.csv(file.path(cef_dir, "bll", "2025", "bll_2025_catches_CEF_v17.1.csv"),
                       na.strings = "")
distribution_data <- read.csv(file.path(cef_dir, "bll", "2025", "bll_2025_distributions_CEF_v17.1.csv"),
                              na.strings = "")

catch_data <- catch_data %>%
  filter(catchCategory != "BMS", fleetValue != "MIS_MIS_0_0_0_IBC") %>%
  derive_fields()
```

The groups below are written against columns of the catch (`metier4`). The
distributions carry none of the stratum columns - the fleet, the area and the
season belong to the catch - so `derive_fields()` hands them back with the same
columns, linked to their catch rows through `domainBiology`:

```{r derive-dist}
distribution_data <- derive_fields(catch_data, distribution_data, what = "distribution")
table(distribution_data$distributionType)   # lengths only
```

The raising is the one of vignette 2, with four groups by gear, each raised
from its own strata:

```{r raise, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
strataCond <- list(
  G1 = quo(metier4 == "TBB"),
  G2 = quo(metier4 %in% c("GTR", "GNS")),
  G3 = quo(metier4 %in% c("OTB", "SSC", "SDN")),
  G4 = quo(!metier4 %in% c("TBB", "GTR", "GNS", "OTB", "SSC", "SDN")))

raised <- catchRaising(catch_data = catch_data,
                       condition_raising_st_list = strataCond,
                       condition_matched_data_list = strataCond,
                       type = "discards",
                       originType = "WGEstimate",
                       variableType = "WeightLive",
                       logFile = file.path(tempdir(), "raising_log.txt"))
```

# Where are the length samples?

The coverage plots take `what = "length"` and the distributions. Landings and
discards are looked at separately (`catchCategory`): the share of the weight
that has a length distribution linked, per metier and mesh, and which strata
clear a floor on both the coverage and the number of fish measured.

```{r cov-bar, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = "Length-sampled versus unsampled landed weight per metier, filled by mesh"}
plot_coverage_bar(catch = raised, distributions = distribution_data, y = "metier4",
                  fill = "mesh", what = "length", catchCategory = "Lan")
```

```{r cov-heat, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Length-sampling coverage of the discards by metier and mesh, with the thresholds in the box under the panel"}
plot_coverage_grid(catch = raised, distributions = distribution_data, y = "metier4",
                   x = "mesh", what = "length", catchCategory = "Dis",
                   thresholds = list(cov = 50, fish = 100))
```

The numbers at length that were sampled, with `plot_NaLoA()` - the plot the
allocation will be looked at with, in the same call. Nothing is estimated yet,
so the title says the distributions are *only sampled*:

```{r sampled-numbers, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Numbers at length of the landings that were sampled, one panel per metier"}
plot_NaLoA(data = raised, distributions = distribution_data, catchCategory = "Lan",
           fill = "metier4", facet = "metier4", scales = "free")
```

A group whose strata are all well sampled can be allocated on its own data; one
that is not has to borrow from a wider pool. That is what the two lists of
conditions say.

# The groups

Like the raising, the allocation takes two named lists of conditions:
`allocStrataCond`, the strata that are allocated together (a group), and
`bioMatchedCond`, the distributions each group takes its shape from. The
second can be wider than the first - a group with too few samples of its own
borrows from a pool that contains them. Here the landings of the three main
gear groups and the discards of the TBB are allocated on their own samples, and
everything else takes all the samples of its catch category:

```{r groups}
allocStrataCond <- list(
  GA1 = quo(catchCategory == "Lan" & metier4 == "TBB"),
  GA2 = quo(catchCategory == "Lan" & metier4 %in% c("GTR", "GNS")),
  GA3 = quo(catchCategory == "Lan" & !metier4 %in% c("TBB", "GTR", "GNS")),
  GA4 = quo(catchCategory == "Dis" & metier4 == "TBB"),
  GA5 = quo(catchCategory == "Dis" & metier4 != "TBB"))

bioMatchedCond <- list(
  GA1 = quo(catchCategory == "Lan" & metier4 == "TBB"),
  GA2 = quo(catchCategory == "Lan" & metier4 %in% c("GTR", "GNS")),
  GA3 = quo(catchCategory == "Lan"),                       # all the landings samples
  GA4 = quo(catchCategory == "Dis" & metier4 == "TBB"),
  GA5 = quo(catchCategory == "Dis"))                       # all the discards samples, TBB included
```

`check_group_conditions()` is what the allocation runs internally before it
allocates anything; running it first is good practice - every stratum is
checked for a gap (claimed by no group) and an overlap (claimed twice). The
column sums say how many rows each group claims:

```{r check, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
cond_st <- check_group_conditions(catch_data = raised,
                                  condition_list = allocStrataCond,
                                  domain = "domainBiology",
                                  logFile = NULL, append = TRUE)
```

```{r check-result}
strata_matrix <- do.call(cbind, cond_st)
cat(sprintf("%d rows in no group, %d rows in more than one (both should be 0)\n",
            sum(rowSums(strata_matrix) == 0), sum(rowSums(strata_matrix) > 1)))
colSums(strata_matrix)
```

# Allocating

```{r allocate, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
allocated <- catchAllocationAoL(catch_data = raised,
                                distribution_data = distribution_data,
                                condition_alloc_st_list = allocStrataCond,
                                condition_matched_data_list = bioMatchedCond,
                                originType_catch = "WGEstimate",
                                variableType_catch = "WeightLive",
                                distributionType = "LengthTotal",
                                variableType_mean = "WeightLive",
                                weighting = "NumberAtAoL",
                                logFile = file.path(tempdir(), "allocation_log.txt"),
                                verbose = FALSE,
                                assembled_output = TRUE)
```

The result is a list: `$distribution`, every distribution of the catch -
the sampled ones as they came, and the ones the allocation estimated for the
strata without samples - and `$catch`, the catch the allocation ran on. A
distribution the allocation estimated carries a domain it made up
(`"[alloc]_..."`) that only this `$catch` knows, which is why both come
together. `sampledOrEstimated` says which is which:

```{r allocated-result}
table(allocated$distribution$sampledOrEstimated, allocated$distribution$catchCategory)
```

# What the allocation did

The plots are the ones that looked at the lengths before the allocation,
`plot_NaLoA()` and `plot_MWaLoA()` (vignette 1), given the two tables of the
result: its `$catch` as the catch and its `$distribution` as the
distributions. It has to be this `$catch`, not the one that went in: the
distributions the allocation estimated for a stratum without samples carry a
domain it made up, and only this `$catch` knows it (the plot warns when it is
missing).

`sampledOrEstimated` is a variable like any other: by default it is the mark -
solid bars where the numbers were sampled, transparent and hatched ones where
the allocation estimated them - and it can be the `fill` or a `facet` instead.
The title says what the distributions hold: *sampled + estimated* here; before
the allocation, as in the plot above, *only sampled* and no mark, because there
is nothing to tell apart. Numbers are in thousands and lengths in cm.

```{r alloc-numbers, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Numbers at length of the landings, solid bars where sampled and hatched where estimated, one panel per metier"}
plot_NaLoA(allocated$catch, allocated$distribution, catchCategory = "Lan",
           fill = "metier4", facet = "metier4", scales = "free", stacked = TRUE)
```

Sampled against estimated as the colour, one panel per metier - the discards,
where most of what is there is estimated:

```{r alloc-numbers-dis, fig.height = 5.5, fig.alt = "Numbers at length of the discards, filled by sampled or estimated, one panel per metier"}
plot_NaLoA(allocated$catch, allocated$distribution, catchCategory = "Dis",
           fill = "sampledOrEstimated", facet = "metier4", scales = "free",
           stacked = TRUE)
```

The mean weight at length, the number-weighted mean of every stratum that
shares the plotted columns - one line for what was sampled (solid, with circles)
and one for what the allocation estimated (dotted, with crosses), side by side:

```{r alloc-mw, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Mean weight at length of the landings, one colour per metier, a solid line for sampled and a dotted one for estimated"}
plot_MWaLoA(allocated$catch, allocated$distribution, catchCategory = "Lan",
            colour = "metier4")
```

```{r alloc-mw-dis, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Mean weight at length of the discards, sampled against estimated, one panel per metier"}
plot_MWaLoA(allocated$catch, allocated$distribution, catchCategory = "Dis",
            colour = "sampledOrEstimated", facet = "metier4")
```

`bin_width` pools the length classes into wider bins (for ages `plus_group`
pools the oldest ages into one class), as before the allocation:

```{r alloc-bins, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = "Numbers at length of the landings in 5 cm bins"}
plot_NaLoA(allocated$catch, allocated$distribution, catchCategory = "Lan",
           fill = "metier4", bin_width = 5)
```

# Adding it up

The plots and the framework's own aggregation, `catchAtAoLAggregation()`, read
the same result, so they cannot disagree. Asked for directly the aggregation
gives the catch-at-length table, one column per length class (as the file has
them), here for the whole catch by category and by what was sampled:

```{r aggregate-n}
numbers <- catchAtAoLAggregation(distribution_data = allocated$distribution,
                                 catch_data = allocated$catch,
                                 grouping = c("catchCategory", "sampledOrEstimated"),
                                 originType_catch = "WGEstimate",
                                 variableType_catch = "WeightLive",
                                 distributionType = "LengthTotal",
                                 round = 0)
dim(numbers)

# six classes spread over the range, small fish (the discards) to large
classes <- grep("^N_", names(numbers), value = TRUE)
shown <- classes[round(seq(1, length(classes), length.out = 6))]
numbers[, c("catchCategory", "sampledOrEstimated", shown)]
```

The plot draws the same numbers: the landings of the plots above, in thousands,
against the landings of the table (which is rounded to whole fish):

```{r agree}
plotted <- plot_NaLoA(allocated$catch, allocated$distribution, catchCategory = "Lan")
c(plot  = sum(plotted$data$number),
  table = sum(numbers[numbers$catchCategory == "Lan", classes]) / 1000)
```

and `meanWoLatAoLAggregation()` the mean weight at length, weighted by those
numbers:

```{r aggregate-w}
meanweight <- meanWoLatAoLAggregation(distribution_data = allocated$distribution,
                                      catch_data = allocated$catch,
                                      grouping = "catchCategory",
                                      weighting = "NumberAtAoL",
                                      originType_catch = "WGEstimate",
                                      variableType_catch = "WeightLive",
                                      variableType_dist = "WeightLive",
                                      distributionType = "LengthTotal",
                                      unit = "g", round = 1)
meanweight[, c("catchCategory", sub("^N_", "W_", shown))]
```

Both take the groups you plot by in `grouping` - any column of the catch or of
the distributions - and a plus group (`plusGroup = TRUE`, with `maxAoL`) for
ages.

# The stock coordination files

The end of the chain: what the raising raised and the allocation allocated,
added up into the two tables of the stock coordination format (SCF v4), Catch
Combined (CC) and Distributions Combined (DC), which are uploaded together.
Both are made from the two tables of the allocation result - its `$catch` and
its `$distribution` - and every field the format has that the data does not
fill is there, empty.

Unlike the plots above, the sums do not need the allocation's own `$catch`: the
raised catch the allocation was run on gives the same tables. A distribution is
linked to its catch through `domainBiology`, and the strata the allocation
estimated a distribution for - which have no domain in the raised catch - through
the `"[alloc]_<season>_<area>_<unit>_<fleet>_<category>"` the allocation made up
for them, which a catch row with none is given too. A catch weight with no
distribution, or a distribution with fish and no catch weight, is warned about:
how much of the catch is not in the numbers, and in which strata.

`catchCombined()` adds the catch up by year, working group, stock and catch
category (`grouping` adds the season, the area or the fleet, when the stock
assessment splits the catch by them). Take the working group's own figures,
`originType_catch = "WGEstimate"`, and a unit the format accepts. The data
cannot say which working group the files are for, so `workingGroupYear` - the
year of the working group that processes them, 2026 for the brill of a WGNSSK
2026 - is an argument, written on every row with the `version`:

```{r scf-cc}
cc <- catchCombined(catch_data = allocated$catch,
                    grouping = "catchCategory",
                    originType_catch = "WGEstimate",
                    variableType_catch = "WeightLive",
                    unit = "t", round = 3,
                    workingGroupYear = 2026,
                    version = 1, versionDescription = "brill 2025 example")
cc[, c("recordType", "workingGroupYear", "version", "year", "stock",
       "catchCategory", "variableType", "variableUnit", "total")]
```

How much sampling stands behind a total is in the format too - `PSU` (the type
of sampling unit), `numPSUs` and `numTrips` - and is taken from the columns of
the catch with the same names, as the CEF has them: the counts of the rows
added up are summed, empty where none of the rows has one, and the rows the
raising only estimated, whose rate was borrowed from a group, leave their
counts out:

```{r scf-sampling}
cc[, c("catchCategory", "PSU", "numPSUs", "numTrips")]
```

`distributionsCombined()` takes the arguments of the two aggregations above and
gives the format's long table: for every length class a `Number` row (thousands
of fish, `NE3`) and a `WeightLive` row (the mean weight, in g) of each catch
category. It adds up exactly as `catchAtAoLAggregation()` and
`meanWoLatAoLAggregation()` do - they are made of the same two functions - and
leaves out the classes no fish fall in:

```{r scf-dc}
dc <- distributionsCombined(distribution_data = allocated$distribution,
                            catch_data = allocated$catch,
                            originType_catch = "WGEstimate",
                            variableType_catch = "WeightLive",
                            distributionType = "LengthTotal",
                            unit = c("NE3", "g"), round = 3,
                            workingGroupYear = 2026,
                            version = 1, versionDescription = "brill 2025 example")
dim(dc)
head(dc[, c("catchCategory", "distributionType", "distributionClass",
            "variableType", "variableUnit", "valueType", "value")], 4)
```

The distributions carry their sampling too: `PSU`, `numPSUs`, `numTrips` and
`numMeasurements`, summed over the distributions a class is made of, each
counted once however many classes it has. The distributions the allocation
estimated were borrowed and have none, so they add nothing; and
`numMeasurements` is the count of the whole distribution, repeated on its
classes, as the CEF has it - do not add it up over the classes.

The format compares each category's catch with the sum of products of its
distribution - the numbers times the mean weights, over the classes - and does
not accept a total more than 20 % off. The same check before the files go
(NE3 times g, in tonnes):

```{r scf-sop}
dc %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c(catchCategory, distributionClass),
                     names_from = variableType, values_from = value) %>%
  group_by(catchCategory) %>%
  summarise(SOP_t = sum(Number * 1000 * WeightLive, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6) %>%
  left_join(cc[c("catchCategory", "total")], by = "catchCategory") %>%
  mutate(SOP_over_catch = round(SOP_t / total, 3))
```

The year is the calendar year here (`calendarYear = "Y"`); a stock whose model
year starts on another date says so with `calendarYear = "N"` and
`startDateYear = "07-01"`, the same in both tables. `write.csv(cc, "CC.csv",
row.names = FALSE, na = "")` writes a table with its empty fields left empty.

# Letting the data choose the groups

The groups above are written by hand. `recommend_groups()` chooses them from
the data, in the same order as for the raising (vignette 2): you name the
variables that matter, from the one that matters most to the one that matters
least, and how well sampled a pool has to be. What
already has a length distribution is kept as sampled (L1, the strata as reported);
the reported strata are summed into strata of the variables you named and tested
before anything else is pooled (L2); the ones that fall short are pooled across
the last variable first, and the variable that matters most is the last to go,
until everything is pooled (All by All). Give it the raised catch and
the distributions: the coverage of a pool is the share of its weight that has a
length distribution, and `fish` the least number of fish measured behind it.
Landings and discards are grouped on their own, so the groups, and their
conditions, say which catch part they are for. The catch part is the last variable
to be pooled across (`drop_catchCategory = TRUE`, the default): the pool of the
whole catch part is tested first, and only what still falls short is allocated
from landings and discards together. `drop_catchCategory = FALSE` keeps the catch
part always - the length distribution of the landings is no use to the discards -
and accepts the pool of the catch part whether or not it reaches the thresholds.

```{r rec-length}
hierarchy <- c("areaValue",          # matters most: the last one to be pooled across
               "mesh",
               "vesselFlagCountry",
               "seasonValue")        # matters least: the first one to be pooled across

rec_length <- recommend_groups(raised, hierarchy,
                               list(cov = 50, trips = NA, fish = 100),
                               distribution_data = distribution_data)
rec_length
```

```{r rec-length-plot, fig.height = 6, fig.alt = "Catch weight of the landings and of the discards allocated at each level of the groups, solid where sampled and hatched where allocated from the pool"}
plot_recommended_groups(rec_length)
```

`rec_length$strataCond` and `rec_length$matchedDataCond` are the two lists
`catchAllocationAoL()` takes, in place of `allocStrataCond` and `bioMatchedCond`:

```{r rec-length-allocate, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
allocated_rec <- catchAllocationAoL(catch_data = raised,
                                    distribution_data = distribution_data,
                                    condition_alloc_st_list = rec_length$strataCond,
                                    condition_matched_data_list = rec_length$matchedDataCond,
                                    originType_catch = "WGEstimate",
                                    variableType_catch = "WeightLive",
                                    distributionType = "LengthTotal",
                                    variableType_mean = "WeightLive",
                                    weighting = "NumberAtAoL",
                                    logFile = file.path(tempdir(), "allocation_log.txt"),
                                    verbose = FALSE,
                                    assembled_output = TRUE)
```

The numbers at length of the two allocations, in thousands of fish:

```{r rec-length-compare}
thousands <- function(a) {
  n <- catchAtAoLAggregation(distribution_data = a$distribution, catch_data = a$catch,
                             grouping = "catchCategory", originType_catch = "WGEstimate",
                             variableType_catch = "WeightLive", distributionType = "LengthTotal",
                             round = 0)
  setNames(rowSums(n[, grep("^N_", names(n))]) / 1000, n$catchCategory)
}
round(rbind(hand_written = thousands(allocated), hierarchy = thousands(allocated_rec)))
```
